messages:
alex: CI error on docs deploy: broken fragment resolver complaining about an empty anchor in /examples/usage.

jade: Any idea which file?

alex: examples/usage.md — we have an inline code example with a leading backtick followed by a heading-like token, e.g. `` `# Example` ``. The markdown parser was turning that into a header in the rendered tree.

noah: Yikes. Fenced inline code should be safe, but some renderers unwrap it when the fence lang is `md` or when MDX compilation trims the fence.

jade: Quick fix: escape the hash `\#` in the inline code or use a triple-fence with `text` and ensure it's not `md`.

alex: I pushed a tiny PR that changes the code fence to ```text and escapes the hash in inline case. Also added a one-line unit in CI to grep for code fences declared as `md` that contain leading hashes.

docs-bot: @alex opened PR #4001 — "docs: avoid md fences that generate headings; escape leading '#' in inline code" — https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4001

ci-bot: docs CI started for PR #4001 (mkdocs/docusaurus checks)

ci-bot: docs CI ✅ build passed and linkcheck clean for PR #4001

noah: Nice. Can we add a short CONTRIBUTING note to prefer `text`/`bash` for code fences that include literal markdown tokens? Save future confusion.

jade: Good call — added a one-paragraph note and a suggested pre-commit snippet to normalize fence languages.

alex: Merged and deployed to staging. Verified example deep links and TOC are fine now.

noah: Closing this thread. Thanks!
